decisions.reason: The bottom-side placement constraint does not change the three-board architecture or the functional roles of the main and sensor boards.
The source context concerns the vertically mounted main and sensor boards; it does not change the power board's mechanical form factor or connector placement.
Component-side accessibility does not alter the power board's four-layer stack or ground-plane strategy.
Minimizing bottom-side placement does not resolve or alter the existing finding that the specified contents cannot fit within the given main-board dimensions.
The reset interface's connector, electrical action, and panel-mounted implementation remain valid; the general board-side layout constraint is owned by the placement Requirement.
The source does not change the charge-status circuit, external LED connector, component population, or indication path.
The signal connector types, references, and pinouts remain unchanged; physical side placement is separately represented by the source Requirement.
The sensor-board connector matrix and total connector count remain unchanged; the source adds only a general physical placement constraint.
The interboard power topology, connector definitions, and pin-order rule remain valid without modification.
The label requirement applies to the power board, while the source constraint is grounded in the downward-facing main and sensor boards; it does not require relocating the power-board labels.
The panel power-button connector's board assignment, signal connection, and behavior remain unchanged; no specific connector-side relocation is entailed.
The bottom-side placement constraint does not alter the monitored rails, INA topology, measurement coverage, or spare-channel count.
